claims.text: The new model will accurately separate lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr.
The model is applicable from 200 K to 1200 K.
The modeled material is HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
The new model accounts for atomic-scale complexity in heat transport.
Atomic-scale interactions and defects are structural mediators of heat transport in the alloy.
The model incorporates temperature-dependent variations in atomic mass.
The model incorporates temperature-dependent variations in force constants.
Incorporating the stated atomic-scale variables will improve thermal-conductivity prediction accuracy.
The new model will improve predictive accuracy by at least 20% relative to previous models.
Previous models do not adequately separate lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions.
The model can predict total thermal conductivity and its lattice and electronic components at 200, 400, 800, and 1200 K.
A deviation of more than 20% between measured and predicted thermal conductivity falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The outcome predicts an improvement of at least 20%, while the uncertainty field says the exact improvement cannot be established without empirical validation; the lower-bound claim is therefore more definite than the stated uncertainty supports.
